title: Small-Cap Liquidity Shocks
market_behavior: Temporary liquidity demand can move small or less-liquid equities more than fundamentals justify.
forced_actor: Funds facing redemptions, stop-loss sellers, concentrated holders, small-cap index funds, and liquidity-sensitive systematic strategies.
why_edge_might_exist: When liquidity is thin, urgent selling can push prices away from fair value and create a later reversal if the original pressure fades.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: The most interesting cases may be too small, too illiquid, too operationally noisy, and too capacity-limited for large funds.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity is expected to be low by design; this mechanism is interesting only if expected personal position size remains small relative to dollar volume.
observable_predictions: Large downside moves with abnormal volume in liquid-enough small names should show measurable short-horizon reversal.
The effect should deteriorate quickly as spread, impact, and position-size assumptions become harsher.
falsification_tests: Reject if the effect fails after conservative spread and liquidity assumptions.
Reject if delisted names or survivorship issues cannot be handled.
Require minimum trade count and liquidity buckets before interpreting results.
references: Academic literature on liquidity risk and short-term reversal
Market microstructure literature on price pressure
